clue.text: The old man's fur is okay

parts.note: the old man is a father, PA, so 'the old man's' gives PA'S
sable is a prized animal fur

explanation.surface: Someone judges Dad's fur coat acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something passable is adequate or acceptable, a synonym of okay.

clue.text: Left bouquet upside-down? That's wrong!

indicators.note: in a down clue, upside-down means the letters of left plus bouquet are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a wine's bouquet is its aroma

explanation.surface: Someone leaves flowers upside down and is scolded for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upside-down' turns LAROMA (L plus AROMA) around. 'bouquet' suggests flowers, but here it is the smell of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoral means lacking any moral sense, so as an adjective it fits wrong in the sense of unprincipled.

clue.text: Meet about trendy French banker

indicators.note: about means the word for meet goes around the word for trendy

parts.note: to meet someone is to see them
in means fashionable or trendy

explanation.surface: A fashionable French financier arranges a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'banker' in crosswords is often a river, which has banks.
explanation.definitionFit: The river flowing through Paris has banks, so it is a crossword-style 'banker' located in France.

clue.text: Aggressive black beagle finally upset collies

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word beagle
upset means the letters of collies are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A fierce black beagle unsettles some sheepdogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellicose describes someone eager to fight, a close synonym of aggressive.

clue.text: Sincere answer received by Hemingway?

indicators.note: received by means the abbreviation for answer is taken inside the writer's first name

parts.note: Ernest Hemingway was the American novelist

explanation.surface: A reply to the novelist Hemingway is heartfelt.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means serious and heartfelt in intention, a synonym of sincere.

clue.text: Surprise a married former President

parts.note: George Bush (either one) was a US President

explanation.surface: A wedded ex-president springs a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: To ambush is to attack from hiding, which takes the victim by surprise; both work as verbs.

clue.text: 'Farewell' bill island's presented by Brussels

parts.note: a bill is a poster or advertisement, AD
Brussels is the seat of the European Union, EU

explanation.surface: A bill for an island is handed over by EU officials as a goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brussels' stands for the European Union, whose institutions are based there.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is the French word for goodbye, used in English as a formal parting word.

clue.text: Work as butcher in city

indicators.note: work here means the letters of as butcher are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone takes a job as a butcher in a city.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Romania is a city, so the answer is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Covered seat occupied by wife and daughter

indicators.note: occupied by means the word for seat has the abbreviation for wife sitting inside it

parts.note: a saddle is a seat for a rider

explanation.surface: A seat was taken by a wife and her daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Swaddled means wrapped tightly in cloth, as a baby is, so it is a synonym of covered.

clue.text: Little woman on the bottle is cheerful

parts.note: Jo March is one of the sisters in Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women
a vial is a small bottle

explanation.surface: A small woman who drinks is merry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the bottle' suggests a drinker; here 'on' simply means placed before, and 'Little woman' points to Alcott's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Jovial means good-humoured and merry, a synonym of cheerful.

clue.text: Actor in a play getting protection from cats and dogs?

indicators.note: play means the letters of actor in a are played about with into a new order

explanation.surface: An actor in a play gets something to keep off cats and dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raining cats and dogs' means pouring with rain, so the definition is a witty way of saying rain protection.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterproof coat protects from heavy rain, which the idiom calls raining cats and dogs.

clue.text: If this rule is transgressed, it's the player's fault

definitions.text: If this rule is transgressed, it's the player's fault

parts.words: If this rule is transgressed, it's the player's fault
parts.note: in tennis, a server who steps over the back line commits a foot fault; 'rule' puns on a line drawn on the court

explanation.surface: Breaking this regulation puts the blame on the player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rule' reads as a regulation, but it is a ruled line; stepping on or over it while serving is a 'fault' in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: The back line of a tennis court is a ruled line; crossing it when serving is called a foot fault.

clue.text: You look, we hear, for African country

indicators.note: we hear signals that the phrase for you look is taken by its sound

parts.note: 'you gander' is you taking a look, gander being slang for a look

explanation.surface: Someone tells you to look for an African nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The East African nation whose capital is Kampala is a country in Africa.

clue.text: After setback, setter perhaps grasps anagram of pedometer as easy to get on with

indicators.note: grasps means the reversed dog holds the rearranged letters inside it
setback means the word for setter perhaps is set backwards

parts.note: a setter is one breed of dog

indicators.note: anagram of openly says the letters of pedometer are to be reordered

explanation.surface: A setter recovering from a setback clings to a pedometer and is friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the crossword compiler, but is the dog breed; 'After' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A good-tempered person is amiable and pleasant, hence easy to get along with.

clue.text: One student wearing yellow is innocent

indicators.note: wearing means the cowardly word has the other letters worn inside it

parts.note: yellow means cowardly, gutless
one is the Roman numeral I
L for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student dressed in yellow is not to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yellow' suggests a colour of clothing, but means cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Guiltless means free from blame or wrongdoing, a synonym of innocent.

clue.text: Model tug made in scale

indicators.note: model as a verb means to shape, so the letters of tug made in are reshaped

explanation.surface: A scale model tugboat has been built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a noun describing the tug, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnitude is size or extent, which is one sense of scale, as in the scale of a disaster.

clue.text: Hold up what might be charged for ride

parts.note: to stall is to delay or hold up
an ion is an atom carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: A delay before something you might have to pay for, such as a fairground ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' suggests a fee, but refers to electric charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A male horse can be ridden, so it is something a rider mounts: an example of a ride.

clue.text: My incendiary instruction

definitions.meaning: the exclamation 'My!' expresses surprise, as does an old British cry of astonishment
an order to ignite a match

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims over an instruction to set fire to things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike a light!' is a dated British exclamation of surprise, like 'My!'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a surprised exclamation and literally a command to ignite a match.

clue.text: Most enormous rat's leg, broken

indicators.note: broken means the letters of rat's leg are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A huge rat has a broken leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Largest is the superlative of large, meaning the biggest, just as most enormous is.

clue.text: Phrase repeated again and again in Roman tragedy

indicators.note: in signals the letters sit inside the words Roman tragedy

explanation.surface: A line keeps recurring in a classical Roman tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a word or phrase chanted repeatedly in meditation, or a slogan said over and over.

clue.text: Reluctant to put on church robe

indicators.note: put on, like a garment, means the church letters are wrapped around the word for reluctant

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
loth is a variant spelling of loath, unwilling

explanation.surface: Someone is unwilling to don a church vestment.
explanation.definitionFit: To robe someone is to dress them, so as verbs the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Animal from Africa seen in European region

parts.note: land can mean a region or territory

explanation.surface: An African creature is spotted in part of Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large antelope native to the African savanna.

clue.text: Track force

definitions.meaning: an American term for a railway line
to push or coerce them into acting quickly

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an American railway and a verb meaning to coerce someone hurriedly.

clue.text: Set that's home to 1, 2, 3 and 4?

parts.note: a wireless set can tune in to the BBC stations numbered 1, 2, 3 and 4, not to the clue numbers

explanation.surface: A set containing the numbers one to four.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers look like cross-references to other clues, but they are the BBC's national stations numbered 1 to 4.
explanation.definitionFit: A wireless receiver, or 'set', carries the BBC broadcasting channels numbered one to four.

clue.text: Flamboyant performer must have time for clubs, being free

indicators.note: must have time for clubs means one letter is swapped for another in the performer's name

parts.note: Liberace was a famously flamboyant American pianist and entertainer
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A showy entertainer wants time off from nightclubs to be at liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must have time for clubs' replaces the C of LIBERACE with T.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate is to set at liberty, which is the verb sense of free.

clue.text: Revise and rearrange a duet to include piano

indicators.note: to include means the rearranged letters take the musical abbreviation inside them
rearrange tells us the letters of a duet are put into another order

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Two musicians revise and rework a duet for piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearrange' turns A DUET into UDATE, which takes P inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To update is to bring something up to date, a synonym of revise as a verb.

clue.text: New journalist follows posh students

indicators.note: follows places the journalist after the other pieces

parts.note: U means upper-class, posh
NUS is the National Union of Students
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A new reporter trails some upper-class students.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unused has never been used, so it is new or fresh.

clue.text: On the course, it's 18 and dry

definitions.meaning: on a golf course there are 18 tees in all

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, TEE TOTAL is the number of tees on an 18-hole golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotal person drinks no alcohol, which is what dry means in this sense.
